chunks: 45 - Musa ibn al-Qasim from Abd al-Rahman who said: He narrated to me Ja'far ibn Musa from Mihran ibn Abi Nasr and Ali ibn Isma'il ibn 'Ammar from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:

We asked him, and he said: 'Regarding the shaving of the back of the head for the Muhrim, if any one of you needs cupping (al-hijamah), there is no harm in it; otherwise, he must adhere to what the one who performs the shaving (al-mustahil) does when he shaves.'
The Sheikh (peace be upon him) said: And he should not dip his head in water, nor cover his head.

key_terms.الْمُسْتَأْهِلُ: The one who shaves (or the act of shaving)
key_terms.حَلْقُ الْقَفَا: Shaving the back of the head
key_terms.لِلْمُحْرِمِ: For the one in Ihram (ritual state)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for a Muhrim regarding shaving the head and covering it during Hajj?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that while cupping (hijama) is permissible for a Muhrim due to medical necessity, the default ruling for removing hair from the back of the head is to shave it completely, mirroring the practice of the Prophet Musa (AS). Shaykh al-Tusi adds the practical detail that the Muhrim must avoid fully submerging the head in water or covering it, distinguishing these acts from the prohibition of cutting hair. This ruling highlights the balance between ease in cases of need and strict adherence to the state of Ihram's sanctity.
